newsitem.title: USA: Luby's Cafeterias CEO commits suicide - police.
newsitem.headline: Luby's Cafeterias CEO commits suicide - police.

text.p: Luby's Cafeterias Inc. President and Chief Executive John Curtis Jr. has committed suicide, leaving a note to lead his wife and police to a Texas motel where they found his body, police said Friday.
Curtis, 58, was found in his motel room with a knife early Thursday morning at a Motel 6 in northwest San Antonio, police said.
"At 6:59 a.m., his wife called it in," Detective Leslie Spiess of the San Antonio police department told Reuters. "The suicide note he left at home said where he was."
Spiess said he was uncertain how long Curtis, who was found face down in the sink, had been dead.
The Wall Street Journal said in its electronic edition Friday that Curtis' wife told police her husband had been having difficulties with the pressures of being chief executive.
Curtis joined Luby's Cafeteria in 1979 and assumed the position of chief executive in January, the company said in a statement issued Thursday.
The company was not immediately available for further comment.
